persona.goal: Understand SQL window functions well enough to rewrite my self-join reports

user_context.background: Data analyst, 3 years writing SQL reports in PostgreSQL
user_context.constraints: Only a lunch break. Practical examples, no full SQL courses. Switching videos wastes my time: two videos at most.

expectations.notes: Tiny budget: 1-3 short videos or a segment of a longer one; must not exceed 30 minutes; must not include a beginner SQL course.

plan.interpretation: In 30 minutes of viewing across at most two videos, the learner understands window functions (OVER, PARTITION BY, ranking, frames, LAG/LEAD) well enough to replace their self-join based reports with window function queries in PostgreSQL.
assumptions: Self-join reports are typically things like previous-row comparisons, running totals, and top-N per group, which map to LAG/LEAD, window frames, and ROW_NUMBER/RANK.
Videos should use PostgreSQL or standard SQL syntax that works in PostgreSQL.
Two videos at most means the plan should favor one comprehensive practical video plus optionally one short complementary video, not many small ones.
No practice time is reserved, so the 30 minutes is all watching.

sub_topics.title: OVER() and PARTITION BY: window vs GROUP BY
sub_topics.why: The learner knows GROUP BY aggregates, so the key mental shift is keeping row-level detail while computing aggregates over partitions, which replaces self-joins to aggregated subqueries.

sub_topics.title: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK for top-N per group
sub_topics.why: Top-N per group and deduplication are common self-join/subquery report patterns that ranking functions replace directly.

sub_topics.title: LAG and LEAD for previous/next row comparisons
sub_topics.why: Comparing a row with its previous or next row is the classic self-join use case, and LAG/LEAD make it a single pass.

sub_topics.title: Running totals and window frames (ORDER BY, ROWS/RANGE BETWEEN)
sub_topics.why: Running totals and moving averages usually require painful self-joins with inequality conditions; frames replace them.

sub_topics.title: Rewriting self-join reports as window function queries
sub_topics.why: The goal is to convert existing reports, so seeing before/after examples of self-join to window function rewrites ties everything together.
